summary: Ephemeral cross-account/bootstrap IAM role for SRE cross-environment debug access (AWS & GCP)
description:
Issue summary:
Request from SRE-runbook team for a short-lived (2 hour) bootstrap role that allows on-call SREs to assume scoped admin-like permissions across specific AWS accounts (prod-core, prod-serving, staging) and a GCP project (prod-ml). Purpose: live troubleshooting of high-severity incidents that require escalated access (kernel-level logs, node-level diagnostics, and access to serving runtime logs).

Impact:
- Reduces time-to-diagnosis for high-severity incidents by avoiding delays while waiting for manual cross-account approvals.
- Must maintain least privilege and strong audit trails to satisfy security/compliance.

Requested outcome:
- A JIT/ephemeral role that SREs can obtain via the existing JIT portal or OIDC broker for a bounded window (default 2 hours, adjustable by approval).
- AWS: assume-role via STS with session tags (redwood:purpose=debug, redwood:runbook_id), MFA enforced, and source IP constraints for corporate VPN IP ranges.
- GCP: workload identity binding to a short-lived service account token with attribute-based conditions (e.g., attribute.redwood_purpose=debug).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) SRE user requests elevated access via JIT portal and selects target: aws:prod-core, aws:prod-serving, gcp:prod-ml.
2) Approval flow triggers Slack approval from oncall manager (can be auto-approved for emergency runs if emergency flag set).
3) Token issued; user runs diagnostic commands that require the elevated permissions
4) Verify CloudWatch / Cloud Audit logs capture AssumeRole/STS tokens and GCP audit logs show workload identity usage.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 - Initial triage (Priya): identified repeated delays during P1 incidents where engineers waited >45m for cross-account access approvals. Suggested ephemeral role to reduce MTTR.

2026-03-11 - Security review (Maya Patel): proposed controls: session tag-based scoping, MFA condition, max-duration=2h, forced key rotation, alert on out-of-hours usage. Risk assessed as acceptable with these mitigations.

2026-03-11 - Infra notes (Ethan): existing SSO/OIDC broker supports ephemeral AWS assume-role flows; GCP workload-identity requires creating a short-lived binding and IAM custom role. Need terraform change in infra repo.
comments: Priya Raman (2026-03-10): Filing request after 2 incidents where cross-account permission provisioning blocked live debugging. Preferred duration: 2 hours. Required resources: access to /var/log/redwood-runtime/* on serving hosts, CloudWatchLogs:FilterLogEvents, EC2:DescribeInstances, GKE/Anthos kubectl-equivalent access for pod exec.

Maya Patel (Security) (2026-03-11): Security ok with JIT model if we enforce: (1) MFA and corporate IP conditions, (2) session tags required and enforced, (3) alerting to oncall-sre channel when role assumed, (4) auto-revoke after 2 hours. Please provide terraform plan and expected IAM policy statements.

Ethan Cho (Infra) (2026-03-11): Drafted terraform PR to add role aws_iam_role.redwood_jit_debug_role and GCP service account binding. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform/pull/4589. Will add CloudWatch log metric filter and SNS alert for assume-role events.

Maya Patel (Security) (2026-03-12): Added requirement for session policies to drop high-risk permissions (KMS Decrypt on production keys) unless explicitly approved via emergency escalation. Add follow-up ticket to review KMS access exceptions.
Ethan Cho (2026-03-12): Provisionally granted scoped role in staging for test. Waiting on security sign-off for prod rollout.
resolution_notes: Pending - partial rollout to staging completed 2026-03-12. Actions taken so far: created terraform changes in infra repo (PR #4589), added CloudWatch metric filter for 'AssumeRole' and a Slack alert integration for the #oncall-sre channel, staged GCP workload identity binding in prod-ml test project. Next steps: security sign-off for prod, finalize session policy to exclude KMS decrypt unless emergency-approved, and add automated audit entry to internal compliance dashboard.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Security to approve final session policy exception for emergency KMS decrypt (owner: Maya Patel).
2) Infra to merge terraform PR and run terraform apply in prod-staging pipeline (owner: Ethan Cho).
3) SRE to validate runbook steps and confirm alerts fire on assume-role events (owner: Oncall SRE rotation).
4) Compliance to add a quarterly audit to review uses of ephemeral roles (owner: Compliance Team).
